composite.rule: Each lever's hazard ratio is taken relative to the population-typical band (not the best band), converted to years with the Gompertz rule (ln HR / ln 2 × 8), and the years are summed onto your calendar age.
assumptions: Levers summed as if independent; in reality sleep, steps and resting heart rate overlap, so the sum likely overstates both costs and credits.
Population-typical bands are the middle quantile of each source cohort, not a matched sample of your age and sex.
Mortality-rate doubling time fixed at 8 years (published range 7–10).

citation.short: Gompertz composite of published all-cause hazard ratios — the framing WHOOP describes for WHOOP Age

fitness_age.rule: Latest wearable VO₂max placed against sex-specific healthy-population norms; fitness age is the age at which 33.1 ml/kg/min is the median.

citation.short: Fitness-age framing: Nes 2013 HUNT / Garmin Fitness Age; norms: Cooper Institute (ACSM)
citation.ref: ACSM Guidelines (Cooper Institute norms) — values to verify against Nes 2013 HUNT table (DOI 10.1111/sms.12032)

assumptions: Wearable VO₂max is itself an estimate from heart rate and movement, not a lab test.
notes: Verify with a lab or field test before acting on it; wrist estimates can sit 3–5 ml/kg/min off.

hrv_age_equivalent.rule: 90-day median nightly rMSSD matched to the female age bin whose median it is closest to.
assumptions: Norms come from 10-s daytime ECG; wearable overnight rMSSD runs higher.
notes: Norm match, not a clock: HRV has no published all-cause hazard ratio per year of 'HRV age'.

levers.label: Sleep regularity (SRI)
levers.rule: Sleep Regularity Index over the last 90 nights (same-state probability for every minute pair 24 h apart, scaled 0–100), placed in Windred 2024 UK Biobank quintiles; all-cause mortality HR relative to the most regular quintile.
assumptions: SRI quintile cut points assumed; pending Windred 2024 supplementary

levers.label: Daily steps
levers.rule: 90-day mean daily steps placed in Paluch 2022 meta-analysis quartiles; HR relative to Q4. For adults under 60 the benefit plateaus around 8,000–10,000 steps/day.

levers.label: Resting heart rate
levers.rule: 90-day median nightly resting heart rate; all-cause mortality HR from the dose–response curve (HR 1.09 per +10 bpm), evaluated relative to the < 60 bpm band.

levers.label: Sleep duration
levers.rule: 90-day mean asleep time (not time in bed) placed against the Cappuccio 2010 meta-analysis: short sleep < 6 h HR 1.12, long sleep > 9 h HR 1.30, relative to 7–8 h.
